mechanism_narrative: ERBB2-EGFR forced-proximity novokine with GS_med linker (~30 Å) drives sustained, ligand-independent transphosphorylation between two highly homologous ErbB family RTKs (ECD asymmetry only ~9 aa). This amplifies SHC1-GRB2-SOS1-mediated RAS-MAPK and GAB1-PI3K-AKT signaling while partially reducing PLCG1 access due to steric crowding at the co-clustered intracellular domains. Unlike H2F (ERBB2-FGFR1) where massive ECD asymmetry (277 aa) sterically excludes PLCG1, the near-symmetric ERBB2-EGFR pair produces a more subtle biased output: sustained pro-survival/proliferative signaling without the qualitative pathway switch. The predicted transcriptional outcome in aged skeletal muscle is upregulation of MAPK/AKT target genes (MYC, CCND1, DUSP6, ETV4) and downregulation of senescence/inflammatory markers (TXNIP, IL32, S100A4, LGALS3).
